claims.claim: Prefer stable technical identifiers when selecting operational logging context.
claims.trigger: Choosing identifying context for logs under the security rule, including cases where limited personal data is operationally needed and permitted.
claims.exceptions: A preference, not an absolute prohibition on permitted PII or a requirement to invent identifiers; required operational context and privacy/security policy still apply.
claims.enforcement_effect: Source preference constrains selection of identifying log context; no executable check established.

baseline_comparisons.reason: Full quote includes prefer stable technical identifiers, but primary registered action lists secret exclusions, conditional PII and level-independent safety without that positive selection preference. Shared location is not semantic coverage.
Replica action likewise registers prohibitions and conditional PII only; ORACLE_LINKED coverage attribution does not separately describe preferred identifiers.

Minimum useful non-sensitive context and needed specific properties may operationally favor identifiers but do not explicitly choose stable technical identity over other equally useful permissible context.

Correlation normalization/propagation concerns request tracing; stable structured property names concerns keys in templates. Neither explicitly registers stable technical values as identifying context. Semantic union retrieval considered identifiers, PII, personal data, context and logging across all record kinds.

claims.comparison_reason: Potential independent preference omitted during atomization, not a proven EXTRA. Normative phrasing is explicit but whether it adds a separate constraint beyond minimum non-sensitive context remains open.
claims.distinguishing_behavioral_scenario: Two log contexts are equally adequate and permissible: a changing non-sensitive display label and an existing stable technical record ID. The minimum-useful-context rules alone do not rank them; this clause favors the stable ID. If baseline contextual minimization necessarily entails that preference, the candidate is covered.
claims.confidence: HIGH exact source and stated preference; MEDIUM independent content; unresolved semantic subsumption
claims.open_question: Is preferring stable technical identifiers an independently falsifiable selection preference, or an elaboration already entailed by the prior minimum non-sensitive logging-context claims?
claims.next_evidence_strategy: Family3 challenge ORACLE_LINKED bundled atomization, then family5 compare equally useful permissible contexts and inspect all logging references for an explicit equivalent; retain uncertainty rather than treating same quote as proof of coverage.
